subject: Agriculture
title: Biochar
description: A micro-lesson that makes Biochar usable.

hook.text: Amazonian farmers created super-fertile 'terra preta' soil 2,000 years ago using charcoal. We're rediscovering their trick.

buildup.text: Biochar is charcoal made by heating organic matter without oxygen. Its porous structure persists for centuries.

discovery.text: Biochar improves water retention, nutrient holding, and microbial habitat—especially in poor, sandy soils.

twist.text: The carbon in biochar is locked away for hundreds of years—it's a permanent form of carbon sequestration.

climax.text: Scaling biochar remains challenging—production costs are high and benefits vary dramatically by soil type.

punchline.text: Ancient Amazonians solved carbon storage 2,000 years ago. We're just catching up.

quiz.question: What is terra preta?
options: Super-fertile Amazonian soil created with charcoal by ancient farmers

details.summary: Biochar is a charcoal-like substance made by heating organic matter without oxygen. When added to soil, it improves water retention, nutrient availability, and microbial habitat while locking carbon underground for centuries. This topic covers its production, uses, and climate potential.
details.whyItMatters: Biochar is one of the few carbon removal technologies that simultaneously improves agricultural productivity. It can store carbon in soil for hundreds to thousands of years while boosting crop yields on degraded land.
takeaways: Biochar is produced through pyrolysis—heating biomass in the absence of oxygen
It improves soil water retention, nutrient holding, and microbial diversity
Biochar can sequester carbon in soil for hundreds to thousands of years

faq.question: How is biochar made and used in agriculture?
faq.answer: Biochar is produced by heating agricultural waste, wood chips, or other biomass at 300-700°C without oxygen in a process called pyrolysis. The resulting porous charcoal is mixed into soil where it retains water and nutrients, hosts beneficial microbes, and stores carbon.

faq.question: What is the connection between biochar and ancient Amazonian soils?
faq.answer: Terra preta (dark earth) soils in the Amazon were created by indigenous peoples who mixed charcoal with organic waste centuries ago. These soils remain remarkably fertile today, demonstrating biochar's ability to create lasting soil improvement.
